IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT INC-2024-87 — High 5xx rate observed on inference-proxy for model rw-13b-quant-v2. Error rate 5xx >= 7% over 3m. Affected tenants: tenant-123 (prod), tenant-987 (prod), tenant-420 (staging). Paging @oncall-sre @alex @sara_p. Logs: https://console.redwood/internal/incidents/INC-2024-87

alex: oncall here, looking. hitting dashboards now. any recent deploys to serving-runtime or routing?

morgan: no deploys in last 2 hours from eng-runtime. I see a spike in attention kernel OOMs around 12:34 UTC on gpunode-33. Could be quant path regression.

alex: ok. quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle offending tenants 2) route traffic off rw-13b-quant-v2 to safer variant rw-7b-safe-v1 or rw-13b-float32 if available 3) disable model variant if traffic routing doesn't stabilize. who can run toggles? @jia can you take routing?\

jia: taking it. first doing rate-limits on tenant-123 and tenant-987 to protect cluster. applying soft quota 50 rps per-tenant while we triage.

(prashant joins)

prashant: raising CS + legal aware. we should prepare a short customer note if we disable a model variant. cs_bot will open tickets.

cs_bot: Support ticket created for tenant-123 #SUP-4521, tenant-987 #SUP-4522. Template: "We are temporarily routing traffic to a fallback model due to increased errors; minimal feature impact expected."

alex: rate-limits applied. observed inbound QPS for tenant-123 dropped from 420 -> 48 within 30s. error rate still elevated but overall cluster load reduced. next step: route 100% of traffic away from rw-13b-quant-v2. Jia, you have control?

jia: running route change now. command:```bash
redwoodctl route update traffic \
  --route inference-prod \
  --set-weight 'rw-13b-quant-v2=0' \
  --set-weight 'rw-7b-safe-v1=1' 
```Executing...```

jia: update applied. verifying metrics...

morgan: infra metrics show GPU memory pressure dropping on gpunode-33. 5xx rate for rw-13b-quant-v2 dropped to 0.6% after 90s. good sign.

alex: can we also mark the model variant disabled in control plane so no new nodes get scheduled for it? do that as well, then we can scale down any warm pools for that variant.

jia: disabling model variant via control plane API now.```

curl -X PATCH "https://controlplane.redwood.internal/v1/models/rw-13b-quant-v2" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"state":"disabled","reason":"INC-2024-87 - auto-mitigate 5xx spike"}'

```

jia: response 200. model state=disabled. no new allocations expected.

prashant: good. CS: please send tenant-123 + tenant-987 a note: short impact, mitigation, ETA for when we will allow re-enable. do not use technical jargon.

cs_bot: Messages queued to CS for review.

alex: quick verification: can developers still call API with explicit model id? we need a fallback policy that maps disabled variants to safe defaults. Check policy:```json
{"fallback_map": {"rw-13b-quant-v2": "rw-7b-safe-v1"}}
```

morgan: fallback mapping is active. requests specifying rw-13b-quant-v2 are proxied to rw-7b-safe-v1 with a header X-RW-Fallback: rw-7b-safe-v1. Logs show ~200 proxied calls.

jia: rolling back traffic weights back to normal is reversible. leaving disabled state until postmortem and a model patch.

alex: action summary so far: rate-limited tenants, routed traffic off variant, disabled model variant, opened CS tickets. next: capture logs, core dumps, attach to INC, notify SRE rotation for deeper debug. prashant — please assess customer impact severity (P1/P2).

prashant: impact classified P2 for now (multiple prod tenants but mitigated). I'll escalate to P1 if customers report degraded SLA.

morgan: collecting GPU traces and quant kernel logs. dumping KV cache profiles. pushing artifacts to incident bucket: s3://incidents/INC-2024-87/artifacts/

alex: can we keep an emergency throttle rule live for 2 hours then reassess? if stable, move to monitoring-only and schedule rollback window.

jia: set ephemeral global throttle:```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood.internal/v1/traffic-controls/throttle \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scope":"global","rate_limit_rps":500,"ttl_seconds":7200,"reason":"mitigation INC-2024-87"}'
```Response 201.

cs_bot: Customer messages sent for tenant-123 and tenant-987. Templates included link to status page and support ticket.

alex: handing off to sara_p for next on-call window — I need to rotate. Sara, you have context and the mitigation steps above. I will paste checklist to handoff.

sara_p: taking handoff. confirmed: rw-13b-quant-v2 disabled, fallback to rw-7b-safe-v1 active, global throttle until 2 hours from now. artifacts path noted. I'll monitor for 30m then update postmortem owner.

prashant: set postmortem owner to alex and morgan for root-cause, cs will co-own customer comms.

alex: thanks — will start draft. final note: do not re-enable rw-13b-quant-v2 until we've validated quant kernel fix in staging and run a canary at 5% for 24h. (reaction :white_check_mark:)

sara_p: acknowledged. will keep channel open for updates.

IncidentBot: Incident INC-2024-87 status -> mitigated. Updated at 1718646499. Timeline and artifacts stored in incident doc: https://console.redwood/internal/incidents/INC-2024-87

morgan: leaving a small follow-up: we should have an automated safety that moves traffic off a model if 5xx > 5% for 60s with auto-fallback to configured safe model. filing infra RFC after postmortem.

alex: agreed. filing RFC after incident. closing live mitigation loop.

sara_p: closing handoff. next update in postmortem doc.
